text.tspan: Hands cultivate a garden with care.
A community garden needs more than seeds and tools. Our neighbourhood project showed that sharing
responsibility and communicating clearly help people work well together.
First, dividing the work gives everyone a way to contribute. We started small: two neighbours brought tools, while
others bought seeds. We also worked out a watering schedule so that the garden was never just one person’s
Second, clear communication helps a group solve problems. When someone forgot to water the plants, we checked
the schedule together. We made the instructions clearer instead of blaming the person, so everyone could follow
The garden taught us two useful lessons: share the work fairly and discuss problems openly. These habits helped
our plants grow and made us a stronger team. Other community projects can benefit from the same approach.
BUILD YOUR OWN · Claim: teamwork needs shared duties and clear communication. Develop each reason with a garden
example. Reconnect both reasons to the claim. Follow the main idea through two supported points. The conclusion brings
both points together without adding a new reason.
